coverage_gaps: Only the PubMed route is available, leaving trial registries, preprint servers, regulatory databases, patent and chemistry sources, subject indexes outside PubMed, and dedicated citation graphs uncovered.
PubMed-only expansion depends on author, title, identifier, and landmark-term searching, so complete backward and forward citation coverage cannot be demonstrated.
Publication and indexing lag around 2024-12-31 may omit recent online-first records or assign dates ambiguously.
The English-information requirement may exclude relevant evidence available only in non-English full text.
Mechanistic evidence may remain concentrated in overexpression systems, peripheral cells, or animal models, limiting inference to endogenous human nigral neurons.
Variant penetrance, effect size, and functional consequences may remain uncertain for rare alleles or underrepresented ancestries.
exclusion_criteria: The record mentions LRRK2 only incidentally and provides no extractable genetic, enzymatic, substrate, physiological, or Parkinson-relevant result.
A proposed substrate or pathway is supported solely by overexpression, prediction, docking, or an unvalidated screening hit without direct LRRK2-dependent evidence.
The study concerns a non-Parkinson condition with no transferable evidence about LRRK2 enzymology, physiological substrates, or relevant pathway function.
The item is an editorial, news report, conference listing, or narrative assertion that supplies no traceable evidence and no usable primary-study lead.
A duplicate or corrected version contributes no distinct data; its identifier linkage is retained while the authoritative version is used for synthesis.
The record lacks enough English information to establish eligibility or accurately extract the relevant evidence.
A variant claim has no verifiable allele identity, population context, segregation, association, or functional evidence relevant to the brief.
inclusion_criteria: Publication date is on or before 2024-12-31 after resolving online-first, issue, and correction dates.
The record directly addresses LRRK2 or the PARK8 locus in Parkinson disease genetics, LRRK2 enzymology, physiological substrate validation, or a disease-relevant downstream mechanism.
Human linkage, sequencing, segregation, association, penetrance, ancestry, neuropathology, or biomarker studies report interpretable methods and outcomes.

Biochemical, structural, cellular, organoid, or animal studies manipulate or measure LRRK2 and include evidence relevant to kinase, ROC-COR GTPase, substrate phosphorylation, or downstream physiology.

Substrate studies provide direct phosphorylation evidence or orthogonal support such as endogenous detection, phosphosite mapping, genetic loss, kinase-dead controls, inhibitor response, or in-vivo validation.
Null, negative, contradictory, replication, correction, and retraction records are eligible when they bear on the strength or generality of a major claim.
Reviews and meta-analyses are eligible for terminology expansion, landmark identification, and synthesis context, while primary records are required for substantive mechanistic claims.
The record has English full text or sufficient English abstract and metadata to determine eligibility and extract the relevant evidence.

question_frame: Target-mechanism frame: for leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) in Parkinson disease, trace discovery from PARK8 linkage and causal-gene identification through pathogenic, risk, and protective variants; compare variant-specific effects on kinase and ROC-COR GTPase functions; identify physiological phosphorylation substrates and implicated membrane-trafficking, lysosomal, autophagic, and immune pathways; and retrieve human genetic, biochemical, structural, cellular, animal-model, endogenous-substrate, replication, null, correction, and retraction evidence that constrains causality, penetrance, substrate generality, and model-to-human translation. Search PubMed from database inception through 2024-12-31 without geographic restriction. Screen peer-reviewed English-language records and records with sufficient English abstracts or metadata; use reviews for terminology and landmark discovery while grounding substantive claims in primary studies. Decision-relevant outcomes are genetic association and segregation, penetrance, ancestry dependence, enzymatic activity, substrate phosphorylation at endogenous abundance, pathway consequences, neurodegeneration phenotypes, and evidence of inconsistency or dissociation among these outcomes.
stop_rules: Execute all 12 planned PubMed query events and preserve each exact query, wave, execution timestamp, requested cutoff, result count, and available provider-version information.

Do not stop discovery until the sentinel set recovers records for PARK8 linkage or LRRK2 gene identification, G2019S disease association, and Rab-substrate discovery; if an anchor is absent, document the failed recall check and use the allocated expansion query.
Stop terminology expansion when every concept block has produced at least one screenable record or its absence has been recorded as a coverage gap.
Within the allocated expansion event, stop adding author or landmark-term branches after two consecutive tested term groups yield no new decision-relevant eligible record.

Stop substrate searching when each substrate retained in the brief has direct LRRK2-dependent phosphorylation evidence and its strongest available endogenous or in-vivo validation and counterevidence have been captured.

Stop variant searching when major causal, risk, and protective classes have evidence for allele identity, population or segregation context, functional interpretation where available, and penetrance or generalizability limitations.
Stop challenge searching only after null or contradictory evidence and correction or retraction status have been checked for every high-impact genetic, enzymatic, and substrate claim.
Stop at the 12-query budget even if saturation is incomplete, and report unresolved evidence needs in coverage_gaps.
Apply the publication cutoff after retrieval when PubMed indexing or date syntax is ambiguous, preserving excluded post-cutoff records in the screening ledger.
Merge records by stable identifiers while preserving every query-to-record occurrence and fail closed when duplicate records contain conflicting bibliographic identities.
